enonce_markdown: Which class of vertebrates is the only one with feathers?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Vertebrates are grouped into five classes: fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals, each with its own external covering.

### Solution

Only **birds (Aves)** have feathers. Fish have scales, amphibians have a moist skin, reptiles have dry scales and mammals have hair or fur. **Answer: A.**

enonce_markdown: A frog has a moist skin without scales and lays its eggs in water. To which class of vertebrates does it belong?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Amphibians live partly in water and partly on land, with a moist skin and jelly-covered eggs.

### Solution

A moist skin without scales and eggs laid in water are features of the **Amphibia**. Reptiles have a dry scaly skin and lay shelled eggs on land. **Answer: C.**

enonce_markdown: Which of the following animals is a mammal?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Classify an animal by its body features and not by where it lives. Mammals have mammary glands, hair and give birth to live young (in most cases).

### Solution

A **bat** has hair, suckles its young with milk and is a flying mammal. A whale shark is a fish, a crocodile is a reptile and a penguin is a bird, even though it cannot fly. **Answer: B.**

enonce_markdown: An animal has a dry body covered with scales, breathes with lungs, has four limbs, lays eggs with leathery shells on land and its body temperature changes with the surroundings. To which class does it belong?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Use the combination of features (skin, breathing, eggs, body temperature) to find the class.

### Solution

Dry scaly skin, lungs, shelled eggs laid on land and a body temperature that changes with the surroundings (poikilothermic) are features of the **Reptilia**. Fish breathe with gills, amphibians have a moist skin and birds are warm-blooded with feathers. **Answer: D.**

enonce_markdown: State three differences between amphibians and reptiles. *(3 marks)*
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Compare the two classes on skin, eggs and development.

### Solution

| Amphibians | Reptiles |
|---|---|
| Moist skin without scales | Dry skin covered with scales |
| Eggs without shell, covered with jelly and laid in water | Eggs with a leathery shell, laid on land |
| Young (tadpoles) breathe with gills and undergo metamorphosis | Young look like small adults and breathe with lungs from birth |

enonce_markdown: A whale lives in the sea, has a streamlined body and flippers like a fish. Which of the following is the best reason for classifying the whale as a mammal and not as a fish?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Classification uses the fundamental features of a group and not features related to the habitat. Features such as a streamlined body arise because of the way of life.

### Solution

A whale **breathes air with lungs and feeds its young with milk from mammary glands**, which are characteristics of mammals. Living in water, a streamlined body and flippers are adaptations to swimming that fish also show, so they cannot separate the two classes. Whales do not lay eggs in water. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: It lives in water and has a streamlined body
It breathes air with lungs and suckles its young with milk
It has flippers that are used for swimming
It lays large numbers of eggs in water
